topics.label: Introduction to cancer therapy
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic provides the opening framing and learning objectives for the lecture on cancer treatments.

topics.label: Conventional cancer treatment modalities
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics discuss primary standard modalities for eliminating cancer and explain the mechanisms, efficacy, and systemic toxicities of surgery, radiotherapy, and cytotoxic chemotherapy.

topics.label: Targeting cancer-specific biological vulnerabilities
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explore therapeutic strategies designed to exploit intrinsic cellular defects in tumors, including hormone dependence, cell cycle checkpoint failures, and DNA repair deficiencies.

topics.label: Kinase-targeted therapies and resistance mechanisms
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics focus on small-molecule inhibitors targeting hyperactivated oncogenic kinases and detail the molecular mechanisms leading to acquired drug resistance and drug addiction.

topics.label: Antibody-based therapeutics
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics describe the design, mechanisms of action, and clinical applications of monoclonal antibodies and antibody-drug conjugates.

topics.label: Cancer immunotherapy and T-cell-mediated strategies
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics evaluate the biological basis of tumor immune surveillance and discuss therapeutic strategies that harness or engineer T cells to target cancer.

topics.label: Current challenges, future directions, and therapeutic perspectives
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics assess the broader landscape of cancer management by examining genomic stratification, historical treatment trends, future therapeutic paradigms, and associated ethical considerations.
